tweets.text:
Twin brothers Muneeb and Sohaib Akhter, of Virginia, were arrested Dec. 3 for their roles in a conspiracy to destroy government databases. The pair allegedly sought to harm the U.S. government and their former employer, a company contracted to host federal databases. 

The indictment alleges that earlier this year, after the brothers had been fired from their jobs, approximately 96 databases storing U.S. government information were deleted. Both men also face other related charges.

We’re proud of our ICE Homeland Security Investigations special agents who worked diligently on this multiagency investigation.

ICE @EROLosAngeles arrested him in San Pedro, CA.

In Mexico, Cadena-Sosa, his family members and their associates lured women and girls — some as young as 14 — to the U.S. with false promises of jobs. Instead, they were prostituted 12 hours a day, six days a week.

A judge ordered him and a partner to pay more than $1.26M jointly in restitution to 16 different victims.
